as_told.title: Nimitz tic-tac case and its infrared footage

plain: In 2004, off the coast of Southern California, Navy fighter jets from the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz reported a strange object nicknamed the Tic Tac, a white oval shape like the mint. The story here is about the video of it, taken with FLIR, short for forward-looking infrared, a heat-sensing camera mounted on a fighter jet. Podcast host Jesse Michels describes it as the famous Tic Tac video, and in another episode says the thermal camera gave the best image of the whole case. A guest named Merrick von Rennenkampf tells what happened next, as he has heard it. According to him, the four crew in two jets went back to the carrier, and a Navy pilot named David Fravor told another pilot, Chad Underwood, that they had just seen something weird. Von Rennenkampf says Underwood was the one who then went out and filmed it, and that there were radar hits too. People tell it because, if the account holds, trained military crews recorded an object they could not explain.
